products.name: Power Transmission & Distribution EPC

outlook.statement: Company will continue to focus on its core strengths particularly Facility Management Services (FMS) and Municipal Solid Waste Management (MSW) business while selectively pursuing profitable and viable opportunities in Engineering Services (ES) Segment.

Management believes that the Company will be able to settle its remaining debts in the due course and in view of the proposed settlement of debt obligations together with the expected increased realisation from the trade receivables, no adjustments are required in the standalone financial statements and accordingly, these have been prepared on a going concern basis.

The Indian EPC industry is expected to maintain a healthy growth trajectory, supported by continued government infrastructure spending, increasing private-sector capital expenditure, industrial expansion, and growing investments across transportation, energy, utilities and other infrastructure segments. Large, diversified EPC companies are expected to see 9–11% revenue growth, supported by infrastructure capital expenditure, healthy order books and faster project execution.

India's overall power market (installed generation capacity) is estimated at approximately 619 GW in CY 2026 and is projected to reach approximately 893 GW by CY 2031, representing a CAGR of approximately 7.6% during 2026-2031. The Government of India has planned transmission infrastructure to integrate over 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030 and over 600 GW by 2032. Approximately Rs 9.15 lakh crore is expected to be invested in transmission infrastructure by 2032.

Global electricity transmission and distribution market was valued at approximately USD 397.99 billion in CY 2025 and is projected to reach USD 410.8 billion in CY 2026 and about USD 580.51 billion by CY 2034, registering a CAGR of 4.42% during 2026-34.

The Group sees strong long-term opportunities in its EPC business, supported by India's expanding power infrastructure, grid modernisation, electrification and telecom network requirements. Will focus on technology-enabled execution, complex infrastructure projects and selective expansion into emerging opportunities such as renewable and associated power infrastructure.

The Group will focus on expanding its FMS presence across corporate, institutional and government clients, while leveraging technology and integrated service capabilities to deliver cost-effective and efficient facility management solutions.

The Group will focus on technology-driven MSW projects, advanced waste processing, resource recovery and waste-to-energy solutions, leveraging latest technologies to enhance operational efficiency, enhance resource recovery and deliver sustainable outcomes.

India's Power T&D EPC market valued at ~USD 14.68 billion in CY 2025, projected to reach USD 35.20 billion by CY 2035 (CAGR ~9.34% during 2026-2035), supported by planned integration of over 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030 and expansion of Inter-State transmission.
India's facility management market projected to witness CAGR of 12.75% during FY2026-FY2033, growing from TAM of USD 54.81 billion in FY2025 to ~USD 138.04 billion by FY2033.
India's solid waste management market valued at USD 13.0 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 21.9 billion by 2034 (CAGR 6.0% during 2026-2034).

The Company will leverage its extensive technical expertise, execution track record, and domain knowledge to actively participate in and bid for new tenders across its core business segments. Strategic focus will remain on securing selective, high-value opportunities in EPC segments of Telecom and Power T&D, while significantly expanding its presence in Facility Management Services (FMS) business over the coming financial years. The Company will also continue to explore opportunities in the Municipal Solid Waste Management sector, with emphasis on projects that are financially viable, scalable, and aligned with its core competencies.

The Company remains committed to the continuous reduction of its debt through prudent financial management, improved operational performance, and constructive engagement with its lending partners. These initiatives are expected to further strengthen the Company's balance sheet, enhance financial flexibility, and create a solid foundation for sustainable long-term growth while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders.

India's resilient economic growth, supported by sustained investments in infrastructure, rapid urbanization, expansion of power generation and transmission networks, increasing digital connectivity, adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies, and the growth of commercial real estate, is expected to generate significant opportunities across the Company's target sectors. The rapid adoption of AI, cloud computing, data-driven technologies and digital services is expected to accelerate demand for data centres, telecom infrastructure, reliable power transmission and distribution networks, and technology-enabled facility management solutions.
